evidence.observation: R0.8 binds: "Each cap that becomes a parameter has a hard maximum fixed in its spec, and a time-bound test at that maximum (standing rule 2)." D4 makes seven limits parameters: "Seven limits `(p1)`: roster cap (default 128, ceiling 4,096), largest budget (1 MiB, 64 MiB), per-file input (128 KiB, 8 MiB), response (128 KiB, ... ceiling 1 MiB), route timeout (30 s, 600 s), route output (1 MiB, 16 MiB), retained file (128 KiB, ... ceiling 64 MiB)." But LH1-C10, the only LH1 timing criterion, names only five: "each limit at its ceiling stays within the spec's time bound: inputs at each roster ceiling load ...; a source at the input-cap ceiling, a response at the response-cap ceiling and a budget at its ceiling each run; a route that reaches the timeout refuses within the timeout plus its grace." The route-output ceiling (16 MiB) and the retained-file ceiling (64 MiB) have no time-bound test anywhere; LH1-C14 (line 370) tests retained-file behaviour (a bound over the cap refuses) but not a time bound at the 64 MiB maximum. Fix 7 was accepted on the basis of widening LH1-C10 to each D4 ceiling; two of the seven are still unnamed.

concerns.recommendation: Name the route-output and retained-file ceilings in LH1-C10 (or explicitly delegate them to the LH1 spec with the shared-test rationale the criterion's last sentence already allows), so R0.8 is demonstrably discharged for all seven D4 limits.
concerns.title: R0.8 time-bound coverage still misses two of D4's seven ceilings

evidence.location: §4 LH1-C14 and LH2-C3 (line 371) vs §10 D4 (line 481) and §2 LH1 'Retained files' (line 242-247)
evidence.observation: LH1-C14 reads: "a run at the response and roster ceilings, with the retained-file cap raised to fit, completes", and LH2-C3 replays "the LH1-C14 run at the response and roster ceilings `(p1)`". But D4 fixes the retained-file ceiling at "64 MiB", and §2 LH1 states the bound rule: "`run()` bounds each file it will retain (each payload holds at most its stage's scheduled sections times the response cap) and refuses if a bound exceeds the retained-file cap." With the response ceiling at 1 MiB and the roster ceiling at 4,096 rows, a literal joint reading (scheduled sections near the roster ceiling, response cap at 1 MiB) yields a bound of ~4 GiB that the 64 MiB retained-file ceiling can never admit — the criterion then looks impossible — while a fixture with few scheduled sections satisfies it trivially; the criterion does not say whether the ceilings are exercised jointly, which LH1-C10 (line 370) only permits "if it says which and why".

concerns.recommendation: State in LH1-C14 (or defer explicitly to the LH1 spec) that the response and roster ceilings are exercised as parameter values with a fixture whose scheduled-section count keeps the retained bound within the retained-file ceiling, so the completion clause is measurable as written.
concerns.title: LH1-C14's joint-ceiling run is unbounded against D4's 64 MiB retained-file ceiling
